summary: 1949 L-4 lookout on a site used for fire watch since 1915, volunteer-staffed in Idaho's Frank Church Wilderness.

access.note: 1.2-mile trail from the Magruder Corridor/Elk City Road; volunteer-staffed, not a rental.

visit.trail_note: 1.2-mile trail from Magruder Corridor/Elk City Road

events.note: Journal entry describes the mountain used as an observation point with a phone line run up it that summer.
First tower, a log cabin with observation cupola, built. NHLR instead dates this to 1938.
Current L-4 ground house with catwalk built on a roughly 5-foot rock base.
Marion Carruthers is the earliest named staffer on record in the sources checked.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register per the research brief.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, April 6, 2018.

evidence.quote: An old journal from 1915 describes Salmon being used as an observation point and a phone line being run up the mountain that summer.

evidence.supports: tent camp with portable alidade on a stump inside a rock wall
evidence.quote: A tent camp was placed on the upper part of the mountain and at the highest point, a square rock wall was built that surrounded a portable alidade on a stump.
The first tower, a log cabin with an observation cupola, was built on Salmon Mountain in 1928.

evidence.supports: 1928 log cupola per Idaho Fire Lookouts
NHLR's differing 1938 date and tent camp/alidade detail
evidence.quote: First developed as a tent camp with alidade, in 1938, it was replaced with a log L-3 cupola with windows around the first floor.

evidence.supports: 1949 L-4 ground house, only one left in area
evidence.quote: This classic 1936 model L-4 ground house with catwalk was built in 1949 and is staffed by volunteers. Salmon Mountain Lookout is the only L-4 ground cab remaining in the area.
It was replaced, in 1949, with the current L-4 lookout on a 5 foot rock base that is still in use.

evidence.supports: staffing history starting 1943, unmanned into early 1980s, Linda Ambelang last paid lookout
evidence.quote: Salmon Mountain Lookout was unmanned for a number of years through the early 1980s, but continues to be staffed today during fire season.

evidence.supports: location in Frank Church Wilderness, south of Magruder Corridor, north view to Selway-Bitterroot
evidence.quote: Located in the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness, less than a mile south of the Magruder Corridor and the Montana Road, Salmon Mountain also looks into the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness to the north of the corridor.
There is a 1.2 mile trail leading to the lookout from the Magruder Corridor/ Elk City Road.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the first cupola tower to 1938; Idaho Fire Lookouts and Wikipedia both independently give 1928. The story notes the disagreement and leans toward 1928 given two independent sources, rather than silently picking NHLR's figure.

notes_for_editor: NHLR's 1938 date for the first cupola tower conflicts with two other independent sources giving 1928; flagged in the story rather than silently resolved. Did not independently verify the NHLR-registered year of 2009 beyond the brief's own record.
